Spirit, venerated, help us,
Protect his sword and his heart so faithfully!
Grieve, my heart, for lost happiness!
Tears, emanated for the hope that fled!
Sorrow is now my only good,
As peris of dew live of tears I so;
And for others be their wellspring, murky,
It's so bright to me like heavenly waters.
O you who are sunning yourselves in the ray of lust,
Sailors on Golden Hopes Flood,
A cloud can draw near to you, the waves threaten you,
The future will bring you dark and grey!
But the scoundrels of the wilderness hit my heart, oh, so heavy.
Apostate tree no longer spares the poisonous breath!
How can you be so sad when you're as beautiful as you, Rezia? You just have to wave your finger and have everything you envy a woman for?
Only one thing could make me happy, and you can't do it; no one can raise the dead.
Then stick to life.
Huon holds me tight...
Try not to go harder?
Shall we bring them back to the ship and sell them in Sicily? I like to exchange them for another one who is not so stubborn.
You're a rough guy, Abdallah. Didn't you see how much passion there is in her? I'm satisfied. Today I got a first taste of how she can love. You have to have patience ...

Far less patient is the wife of Almansor, Roshana. She has observed the beautiful slave Huon at work in the palace garden and has fallen into intense passion for him, Abdallah, sent by her, whispers to Hüon secretly that a beautiful woman of blood wants to see him, and tells him how he can get from the garden, without notice, into Roshana's garden. In the belief that this is a sign of Rezia, Hüon rushes into the palace. However, he does not meet Rezia, but rather Roshana, who confesses to him her love. As Hüon, he complains that he loves only one woman in the world, Rezia
For you beauty has embellished itself,

Before the rose withers, before the wine is shed!
Go away, the flowers that you praise,
Toxin circling in the cups,
And of the cup of purple,
Looks like I'm blushed with blood.
When women's eyes glow,
Can you shy away from this magic light?

When a white arm flips you?
If you can escape, yes, you can escape,
When a white arm flips you?
No woman's eye greets,
The flame burning with sensuality;

If the soul that takes it escapes from it.

Remember the wise man who wrote of the meal:

So, mortal, rejoice! Be happy! Laugh at the one who sees,
That life is a shadow, and waits until it flees.

O siphon him out! The Blum' picked,

Oh, sip him out, pick the Blum'!

Huon is getting away from Roshana and wants to escape - but too late: Almansor discovers him! Slaves seize him, and the Emir determines his death: He shall be burned at the stake! Huon's fate seems sealed. On the market square of Tunis a large wooden kick is built. A ghastly crowd, among them Scherasmin and Fatime, flocks together, the Emir with his entourage - next to him the veiled Rezia - have taken place on a show frame. Then Abdallah pushes through the crowd ...
Lord, I must speak to you.
Every word of a ruler means a deed, and I'd rather not wish you, Abdallah, that I'm acting now.
This is what I want now, noble prince.
We need to negotiate something.
Not here, not now.
Right here and right now, you'll never get away with it so cheaply, Emir.
These three boxes were thrown to the beach today by the flood.
Everything the sea throws to the beach is mine.
Jewelry! In both boxes! Poor Abdallah! What shall you and your sailors do with jewelry? You cannot let your ears pierce and carry rings in them.
There's something for you, Abdallah.
A beautiful work of art.
A children's trumpet!

How well you behave. A world man and art connoisseur like you! You come to all the big markets. To Sicily, to Rome and Greece. You know very well that this is an invaluable piece. You can exchange it everywhere for whole mountains of gold.
Take the horn, Abdallah, and go before I rejoin this comparison.
Do you want me to blow a song to your glory?
You just have to be careful that you keep your head on your shoulders long enough to play music like that...
I understand, great Emir, and I'm leaving.
There's the pathetic beggar.
Worthless stuff, but I'll take it.
That's the magic horn.
Adjustment, fatime, adjustment ...
Bring the slave I sentenced to death, and tie him to the stake.
Almansor!
What do you want, Rezia?
Mercy - for this man.
He has penetrated into my harem and is penetrating his passion for Roshana. What do you have to do with him?
He's Huon, my husband.
He can't die!
Do you want to share his fate even though he cheated on you?
I'd rather die with him than live without him.
You will soon hear how little he deserves this foolish fidelity.
Come here, slave!
Are you talking to me, Emir von Tunis?

Listen carefully, slave, I'll release you! Abdallah will drop you off somewhere on the coast of your homeland and Rezia will stay with me. You will return as a free man and you can marry whoever you want.
I have never loved anyone other than Rezia, and I die with her blissfully if I am not allowed to live happily with her.
We are a single piece from the Creator's hand. Nothing can separate us!
